notes.50v.1: Lines 50v.2-50v.7 give the opening words of the Mass chants and prayers, translated as quoted. The Gospel words ('whoever says to this mountain') are from Mark, though the rubric says Luke. *sunnestâp* (50v.9) is kept as the text names it; probably 'suone-stap', a staff of settlement or judgement. The fore-oath (voreeit) is the accuser's preliminary oath. 50v.24: 'inprincipioe.. u..' is the abbreviated opening of John's Gospel, 'In principio erat verbum'. Konrad and Rudolf are the formula's sample names.

nodes.text: On the day on which those accused of some crime are to be tried, first this Mass
is to be said: 'You are just, O Lord.' Collect: 'Grant, we beseech you, almighty [God].' Lesson from the prophet Isaiah: 'In those
days the prophet Isaiah spoke, saying: Seek the Lord while he can be found.' Gradual: 'Keep
me.' Alleluia: 'Lord, [our] refuge.' Gospel according to Luke: 'At that time, looking
at his disciples, Jesus said to them: Truly, truly I say to you that whoever says to this mountain.'
Offertory: 'Out of the depths.' Secret: 'Us from all guilt.' Communion: 'Truly I say to you.' Postcommunion: 'United in spirit,
O Lord.' When the Mass is finished, they go to the water where the accused are to be tried. And when the water
has been blessed and the accused adjured, both accuser and accused are set together
beside that water, facing east, each holding in his hand a staff which is called *sunnestâp*,
the priest beginning these words and the accuser repeating them: 'Konrad,
or whatever your name is, I bring a charge against you over my horse that was stolen
from me. I accuse you of having stolen it, and I ask you for God's sake
and for justice's sake to give it back to me. And if you accuse me
besides of pressing my own wanton will against you, then I offer
you my fore-oath on it.' Let the accused answer: 'The fore-oath
I will waive for God's sake, so that he may be the more gracious to me in this
my right.' And let him add these words: 'As Rudolf, who stands here
present, has accused me over his horse, that I stole it
from him: that I have not done, and I offer him for it a lawful
denial in his presence at this blessed water, if he
will accept and trust it.' The accuser answers: 'I accept and trust [it]
and put [it] into your hand, to be performed for me just as you have here
pledged to me.' Afterwards the boy who is to be put into the water in place of the accused, signed
with the Gospel 'In the beginning was the Word', is to be set beside the accused, and the priest is to say
these words: 'This Christian person I lend to you, so that he
may stand in for you at this judgement of God, as you yourself should. So
do I also, and I demand a pledge.'
